landing.subtitle: A single-user control plane that turns CLI agent sessions into a durable loop: goal → execution → completion record → human review → delivery. You define the gates; agents do the work; the platform tracks state and evidence.
landing.mentalModel: A goal is a work item and the sole holder of state authority; a run is one agent's turn on it — runs report up, never decide. The platform judges completion; you hold the gates.

lines.text: linked to daemon (machine=m4.local, 3 agent CLI(s) probed)
ouroflow create goal --title "refactor intake parser" --assignee claude
goal g7a3 created → run r9k1 queued
# platform tracks state + human review; you only appear at checkpoints

loop.title: A loop with a real review gate
loop.desc: Goals, runs, isolated worktrees, completion records, human review, and delivery only after approval (merge + re-verify + push).

acceptance.title: HITL / HOOTL per goal
acceptance.desc: Choose HITL (default: review before delivery) or HOOTL (finish directly; repo-backed HOOTL is not auto-merged) when you create the goal.

subgoals.title: Sub-goals with changes
subgoals.desc: Split work into sub-goals (own assignee, own worktree); verified sub-goals produce Changes with revisions the owner integrates.

collab.title: Four collaboration behaviors
collab.desc: Comment / Consult / Handoff / Sub-goal, exposed as the ouroflow CLI with owner-only permissions enforced server-side.

protocol.title: Multi-protocol & transport
protocol.desc: ACP / JSONL / JSON-RPC over stdio / ws / tcp; agents can carry their own extra MCP servers.

ui.title: Real-time web UI
ui.desc: Live event stream, execution timeline, sub-goal / change / verification panels, and per-agent ACP chat.

landing.prereq: Prerequisites: Go 1.26+, Node.js 20+, npm 10+, Git, and an ACP-capable agent CLI.
firstGoal: Create a domain (project): a repo URL or a scratch workspace.
Create an agent from a runtime detected by ouroflow connect.
Run ouroflow connect on your machine — the daemon dispatches runs via run.poll (pull model).
Create a goal, assign it, choose HITL/HOOTL, and watch: execution → review (human) → delivery after approval.
Or chat with any agent from the Agents page — a per-agent ACP session staged fresh every open.

arch.title: Architecture
arch.intro: Single process, single machine, single user, no auth. Local SQLite for state, in-process event bus, Go daemon + Next.js web UI.

layers.title: Event ≠ truth
layers.desc: The bus is a wakeup hint; every transition is a conditional DB transaction, idempotent under replay.

layers.title: Machine executor (PULL)
layers.desc: ouroflow connect holds a persistent JSON-RPC link and pulls work (run.poll). It executes runs and hosts the per-agent chat bridge — spawns the CLI, relays ACP frames unparsed.

layers.title: Per-run worktrees
layers.desc: ~/.ouroflow/runs/<runID> ephemeral git worktrees against per-domain bare repos. Crash recovery replays terminal runs and re-derives attention at startup.

layers.title: Coordinator
layers.desc: Derived OwnerAttention (integration / recovery / user_action) wakes the owner exactly when there is work for it — never on noise.

stack.stack: Go 1.26, SQLite (modernc), gorilla/websocket, robfig/cron, MCP go-sdk
Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, TanStack React Query

concept.title: Core concepts
concept.intro: The vocabulary of ouroflow — a goal is the sole holder of state authority; everything else reports up.

items.name: Goal
items.desc: A work item. The sole holder of state authority — runs report up, never decide.
items.example:
$ ouroflow create goal --title "refactor intake" --assignee claude
goal g7a3 created → run r9k1 queued

items.name: Run
items.desc: One agent's turn on a goal. No authority — it reports to the goal layer.
items.example:
$ ouroflow goal list
  g7a3  active   refactor intake   [claude]
  g6f2  review   fix feishu stream  [opencode]

items.name: Domain
items.desc: A repo-backed or scratch workspace. The acceptance level is chosen per goal.
items.example:
$ ouroflow create domain --name demo --type repo \
    --git_url git@github.com:org/repo

items.name: Runtime
items.desc: A launch spec — transport + provider + executable/args + env.
items.example:
# transport: stdio | ws | tcp
# provider: acp | jsonl | jsonrpc
opencode acp --pure

items.name: Agent
items.desc: A runtime + persona (system prompt / model / env / MCP servers / concurrency).
items.example:
$ ouroflow agent create --runtime opencode \
    --system-prompt "You are a careful reviewer"

items.name: Chat
items.desc: A direct ACP conversation with an agent. Daemon relays frames unparsed to the CLI.
items.example:
GET /agents/{id}/acp  →  WebSocket
# frames flow unparsed both directions

items.name: Squad
items.desc: A routing group that does no work itself — goals route to its leader, who delegates via sub-goals.
items.example:
$ ouroflow squad create --name review-team \
    --leader claude --reviewer opencode

items.name: Sub-goal
items.desc: A work item split off a goal (no recursion). Own assignee + optional agent verifier.
items.example:
$ ouroflow subgoal create --parent g7a3 \
    --title "add tests" --assignee opencode

items.name: Change
items.desc: A sub-goal's logical deliverable. Owner integrates via the integrate_change tool.
items.example:
$ ouroflow change integrate ch9f2
# conflict → assignee rework → revision N+1

items.name: Verifier
items.desc: A named agent issuing structured verdicts (verify_sub_goal). No built-in domain test runner: put the check in the brief or add a verifier agent.
items.example:
# verifier agent: verify_sub_goal → pass/fail
# the platform does not run domain test commands

items.name: Gates
items.desc: Human checkpoints: HITL review on a goal, gate nodes in a Blueprint.
items.example:
# HITL: goal parks at review
# approve → goal:approved → merge + re-verify + push

items.name: Mention
items.desc: The Consult primitive — a structured URI in a comment pulls an agent into a read-only guest run.
items.example:
$ ouroflow goal comment --text \
    "[@opencode](mention://agent/a4) is this safe?"

items.name: Schedule
items.desc: A cron template that clones a goal per firing. Idempotent, timezone-aware.

collab.title: Collaboration
collab.intro: Agents coordinate exclusively through the ouroflow CLI (a shim of the daemon binary, on the agent's PATH at spawn). Every command carries the per-run token (OUROFLOW_TOKEN), which the daemon resolves to the run's (goal, agent, role) — the token is the ONLY identity, self-reported ids are ignored, and the handoff owner check is enforced server-side.

behaviors.name: Comment
behaviors.desc: Say something on a goal — visible to all participants. The baseline interaction; no permission needed.
behaviors.example: $ ouroflow goal comment g7a3 --text "blocker: tests flaky on CI"

behaviors.name: Consult
behaviors.desc: Pull another agent into a read-only guest run via a mention URI. The requester resumes automatically after the answer lands.
behaviors.example:
$ ouroflow goal comment g7a3 --text \
    "[@opencode](mention://agent/a4) is this refactor safe?"

behaviors.name: Handoff
behaviors.desc: Transfer goal ownership to another agent. The owner check is enforced server-side — only the current owner can hand off.
behaviors.example: $ ouroflow goal assign g7a3 opencode --note "you own the parser now"

behaviors.name: Sub-goal
behaviors.desc: Split work off a goal — own assignee, own worktree, optional verifier. Not a child goal (no recursion). Machine retries ≤3.
behaviors.example:
$ ouroflow subgoal create --parent g7a3 \
    --title "add integration tests" --assignee opencode

collab.tokenNote: The per-run token (OUROFLOW_TOKEN) is the ONLY identity — self-reported ids are ignored, and the owner check is enforced server-side.
